concept.name: Value factor
concept.definition: A Fama-French stock factor measuring the return difference between high book-to-market (value) and low book-to-market (growth) stocks: HML (High Minus Low) is the average return on the value portfolios minus the average return on the growth portfolios.
concept.intuition: It captures the long-documented pattern that stocks cheap relative to their book value have on average outperformed expensive 'glamour' stocks.
concept.mechanics: Within small and big size groups, stocks are sorted on book-to-market equity; HML = (1/2)(Small Value + Big Value) - (1/2)(Small Growth + Big Growth), using value-weight portfolios. A positive HML month means value stocks beat growth stocks.
concept.formula: HML = (1/2)(Small Value + Big Value) - (1/2)(Small Growth + Big Growth).
concept.failure_modes: Value strategies suffer long drawdowns (e.g., the growth-dominated 2010s), and in the five-factor model HML becomes largely redundant once profitability and investment factors are included; whether the premium is risk compensation or mispricing remains unsettled.
concept.misconceptions: The value factor is not the same as buying low P/E 'bargains' by any metric: HML is defined specifically on book-to-market equity within the Fama-French construction, and different value definitions can behave differently.
concept.example: If in a month the two value portfolios average 1.8% while the two growth portfolios average -0.2%, HML is +2.0%, and a fund with HML loading 0.5 gains about 1.0% from the factor.

citations.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library, Description of Fama/French Factors
